key_concepts: Earth revolves around the Sun at 108,000 km/h
Earth's orbit is elliptical, not a perfect circle
Earth completes one orbit in about 365.242199 solar days
Earth travels about 940 million km during one orbit
Perihelion is Earth's closest point to the Sun; aphelion is farthest
Average Earth-Sun distance is 149.6 million km
Earth's axis is tilted 23.5° from vertical
Earth's axis remains fixed and points toward Polaris
Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the Sun in June and away in December
Solstices occur at maximum axial tilt; equinoxes when tilt is perpendicular
The Sun's height in the sky changes with seasons due to Earth's fixed tilt
The subsolar point is where the Sun is directly overhead at solar noon
